clue.text: Dishonest persons give sup ' port to shepherds

definitions.meaning: criminals or swindlers, people who are bent
a shepherd leans on a hooked staff, which holds him up

explanation.definitionFit: Swindlers are called by this word, and the same word names the hooked staffs a shepherd leans on.

clue.text: Daily careful about the youngster

definitions.note: a daily is a cleaning woman who comes in each day

indicators.note: the word for careful is placed around the youngster, so it goes about him

parts.note: chary means wary or careful
a lad is a boy or youngster

explanation.surface: Someone is told to linger cautiously around a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. 'Dally' is an OCR misreading of 'Daily': in Britain a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a British cleaning woman, the same domestic worker as a char.

clue.text: In accordance with, etiquette, but not at one's best

definitions.text: In accordance with, etiquette, but not at one's best

parts.words: In accordance with, etiquette, but not at one's best
parts.note: the clue reads as not agreeing with proper etiquette, and as an athlete or performer below their usual standard

explanation.surface: Someone well-mannered who is having an off day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' is both etiquette (good form) and fitness, so being outside it is both a breach of manners and being below one's best.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsman lacking fitness or touch is said to be off his game, below his usual standard.

clue.text: Hypocrisy we hear from a philosopher

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for hypocrisy is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: cant is insincere, hypocritical talk

explanation.surface: Someone hears double standards coming from a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says CANT is spoken, and it sounds like the German philosopher Immanuel KANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanuel Kant was the eighteenth-century German thinker behind the Critique of Pure Reason.

clue.text: Expression in America means the end for the commuter

parts.note: a term is a word or expression
US is short for the United States, America

explanation.surface: An American phrase meaning the last stop on a daily journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' is a link word, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The final station of a line is where a commuter's train journey ends.

clue.text: An adventure to avoid about this period

indicators.note: the word for avoid is placed around the period, so it goes about it

parts.note: to escape something is to avoid it
AD, anno domini, names the present era

explanation.surface: An exploit undertaken to dodge something at the present time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'this period' is the present era, anno domini.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous exploit, a wild adventure.

clue.text: Justice a wise man treats differently

parts.note: magi, the wise men from the East, here taken as a wise man

indicators.note: treated differently, the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge whom a sage handles in an unusual way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' is the anagram signal. The Magi are the wise men of the Nativity, taken here as one of them; a Justice of the Peace is a lay magistrate in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice is a judicial officer, as a magistrate is in a lower court.

clue.text: Bible portion contains one musical composition

indicators.note: the letters for the Bible portion hold the next word inside them

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a portion of the Bible

explanation.surface: A passage of scripture includes a single piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' is the container signal; 'Bible portion' is the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a piece written for nine players or singers.

clue.text: " Comes the blind Fury with th abhorred-" (Milton)

definitions.text: " Comes the blind Fury with th abhorred-" (Milton)

parts.words: Comes the blind Fury with th abhorred-
parts.note: a line from Milton's Lycidas missing its last word, the tool with which Fate cuts the thread of life

explanation.surface: A quotation from Milton with its final word left for the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton's Lycidas reads 'Comes the blind Fury with th' abhorred shears, / And slits the thin-spun life'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lycidas the Fate Atropos cuts the thread of life with a pair of cutting blades.

clue.text: The joint for a titled person

definitions.meaning: a ... of beef is a large joint of two sirloins
a peer of the lowest rank in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a large cut of beef and also a nobleman of the lowest peerage rank.

clue.text: A number in the money get an aerial

indicators.note: the number is placed in the word for money

parts.note: an anna was a coin of India, one sixteenth of a rupee
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone sets a sum within a cash figure to obtain a radio mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; the anna was an old Indian coin, a sixteenth of a rupee.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio or television aerial is the same receiving rod Americans call by this name.

clue.text: Commander with information goes to church with urgency

parts.note: CO stands for commanding officer
gen is British slang for information
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An officer with intelligence hurries to church.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information; CE is the Church of England. 'Urgency' here means forcefulness, as of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Cogence is the compelling force of an argument, its power to press and persuade.

clue.text: Abandoned — it is not right

definitions.meaning: the side opposite the right hand

explanation.definitionFit: Something forsaken was walked away from, and the side opposite the right is the other side.

clue.text: Moor's topic about one in the printer's

indicators.note: turned about, the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Othello's subject turns up somewhere in a printing works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges MOORS and TOPIC. The apostrophe's S counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor set type by hand in a printing works.

clue.text: Competitor satisfied about the confused thanks

indicators.note: the word for satisfied goes around the next piece

parts.note: content means satisfied

indicators.note: confused says the letters for thanks are jumbled

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, made plural

explanation.surface: A rival is pleased about some muddled gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' jumbles TAS (British 'ta' for thanks, made plural) into STA, and 'about' puts that inside the word for satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: A contestant is anyone taking part in a competition.

clue.text: Scold doctor with work that, gets no return

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: return says the word no is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone tells off a physician whose labour brings no profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses the word no. To drop on someone is an old British idiom for scolding them.
explanation.definitionFit: To come down on someone is to rebuke them sharply.

clue.text: To get this period to come into line needs skill

parts.note: AD, anno domini, names the present era
soldiers dress when they align their ranks

explanation.surface: Getting this era into order takes ability.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'dress' is the military order for troops to straighten their line.
explanation.definitionFit: Address in the old sense is dexterity or adroitness in handling things.

clue.text: Abel's turn to be an officer

indicators.note: to be says these letters are going to become something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Abel's turn has come to hold a commission.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ABEL'S and TURN, nine together, are rearranged; 'to be' signals they become the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British Army a subaltern is a junior commissioned officer below captain.

clue.text: One who absconds with a worker in the bar

indicators.note: the worker is placed in the bar

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise
the worker ant

explanation.surface: Someone flees with a labourer to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub but is a prising tool; 'in' is the container signal. A levanter, in British usage, bolts leaving bets or debts unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A levanter is someone who runs off leaving debts unpaid.

clue.text: People in principle make a brat, dwelling-house

indicators.note: the people are placed in the principle

parts.note: a tenet is a principle
men are people

explanation.surface: Folk with ideals form a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'make a brat' seems to be a misprint in the source and is left as link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a building divided into rented flats or dwellings.

clue.text: Afflicted with a hand in the money

indicators.note: the hand is placed in the money

parts.note: a sen is a small Japanese coin
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Someone suffers when one hand is in the till.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; the sen is a small Japanese coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stricken by disease is afflicted with it.

clue.text: A quarter with board is constant

parts.note: S for south, one quarter of the compass
a table is a board

explanation.surface: A district providing meals stays steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter' is a compass point, S for south; 'board' is TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is steady and unchanging.

clue.text: We need a long, time to notice proverbs

parts.note: an ad is a notice
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: We need lengthy spells to observe old sayings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We need' and 'to' are link words; the notice comes first in the answer, the long time after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Adages are old sayings, proverbs.

clue.text: Gets the Reds together before the break

definitions.text: Gets the Reds together before the break

parts.words: Gets the Reds together before the break
parts.note: in snooker the red balls are packed in a triangle before the opening shot

explanation.surface: Someone organises Communists before a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker's red balls are set up in a triangle before a frame starts with the break-off shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden triangle that holds the reds in place before the break shares the name of a game of snooker.

clue.text: "Be off, or I'll kick you — " (Lewis Carroll)

definitions.text: "Be off, or I'll kick you — " (Lewis Carroll)

parts.words: Be off, or I'll kick you
parts.note: the last line of Father William in Alice in Wonderland, missing its final words

explanation.surface: A quotation from Carroll with its last words left for the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: Father William ends: 'Be off, or I'll kick you down stairs!'
explanation.definitionFit: Father William threatens to kick the young man to the lower floor.

clue.text: Sounds crazy, but he has an Oscar

indicators.note: sounds says the word for crazy is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: wild means crazy

explanation.surface: Someone sounds mad, yet has won a film award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' makes WILD a sound-alike for the writer Oscar WILDE; the Oscar is his first name, not the film award.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright of The Importance of Being Earnest had the first name Oscar.

clue.text: Hint about a beginner — you're looking at it

definitions.text: Hint about a beginner — you're looking at it

parts.words: Hint about a beginner — you're looking at it
parts.note: the solver is reading a puzzle hint at that moment

explanation.surface: A tip for a novice that is already in front of the reader.
explanation.walkthrough: Any crossword solver is at that moment reading one of these hints.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue is a hint that points towards a solution, as in a crossword.

clue.text: One in the chosen race answers back

definitions.note: a reverberating sound repeats a call back to the caller; the clue gives a verb phrase

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A member of the elect people replies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in' signals the letters inside 'thE CHOsen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound repeats a call back, so the mountains seem to reply.

clue.text: Insect bound to annoy the suitor

indicators.note: bound to says the insect is tied on after the word for annoy

parts.note: to gall is to annoy
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug is sure to irritate a wooer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' means tied on, so the insect is fastened after the word for annoy; 'the suitor' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant is an old word for a lady's admirer or wooer.

clue.text: Teach me about the cleaver

indicators.note: turned about, the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be instructed on a butcher's chopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TEACH ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife for chopping through brush, a cutting blade like a cleaver.

clue.text: The heavyweight aboard perspires

annotationWithheld.why: The heavyweight aboard perspires: WELTER inside SS, but 'aboard' is both the container and the only source of SS (on a steamship), one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Numbers turn to catch the poem

indicators.note: turn says the abbreviation for numbers is read backwards

parts.note: to net is to catch

explanation.surface: Lines of verse change position to snare a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses NOS to SON; 'Numbers' also means verses, a misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a fourteen-line poem.
